exposure: Preterm premature rupture of fetal membranes
Mode of delivery management for preterm premature rupture of membranes (PPROM): expectant management vs. active management (delivery 24 hours after second steroid dose)
outcome: Composite neonatal outcome: neonatal death, periventricular leukomalacia, intraventricular hemorrhage, sepsis, oxygen requirement at 36 weeks, necrotizing enterocolitis
cohort: 139 women with PPROM at 28-32 weeks gestation
finding: No significant differences were found between expectant management and active management for the composite neonatal outcome in women with PPROM at 28-32 weeks gestation, although the study was underpowered.
mod_finding: Active management resulted in a higher cesarean delivery rate compared to expectant management (80% vs. 60%).
